title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-1
notes:
West leads the ♥9 against 6♥. West's trump lead is won by South. West's unusual no trump has shown at least 5 cards in both diamonds and clubs. As East bid diamonds, he must have longer diamonds than clubs, making a club ruff prone to an overruff.

South must hope that West is 1156 with the ♦A and ♣Q. The ♦2 is played, forcing West to duck. North wins the ♦Q. South draws trump, pitching a diamond from dummy on the last round. South now cashes 3 rounds of spades, ending in the dummy. A spade is played and ruffed by South. West must keep the ♦A and 3 clubs.

South exits the ♦K to West's ♦A. West must lead a club away from the ♣Q. Even if West plays the ♣Q, blocking the suit, dummy will be high. This ending would not have worked if South had not gone to the trouble of setting up a spade winner in the dummy.
